question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Tranquebar – Location and Features]
options: Tranquebar – Located on the Coromandel Coast of South India
Tranquebar – Acquired by the Danes in 1620 from the Nayak of Tanjore
Tranquebar – Also known as Trankebar by the Danes
wrong_fact: Tranquebar is located in present-day Tamil Nadu (on the Coromandel Coast), NOT in Kerala. Kerala lies on the Malabar (western) coast.
explanation: Tranquebar (Danish: Trankebar) is situated on the Coromandel Coast of South India, in present-day Tamil Nadu. It was acquired by the Danish East India Company in 1620 from the Nayak of Tanjore. Option 4 is incorrect — Tranquebar is in Tamil Nadu, not Kerala.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Tranquebar – Historical Associations]
options: Tranquebar – Site of Fort Dansborg built by the Danes
Tranquebar – Served as the headquarters of the Danish East India Company in India
Tranquebar – Base for the first Protestant missionary activity in India (Ziegenbalg)
Tranquebar – Ceded to the French East India Company in the 18th century
wrong_fact: Tranquebar was never ceded to the French East India Company. It remained under Danish control until it was sold to the British East India Company in 1845.
explanation: Fort Dansborg was built by the Danes at Tranquebar and served as the Danish EIC headquarters in India. Bartholomäus Ziegenbalg arrived at Tranquebar in 1706, launching the first Protestant missionary activity in India (Tranquebar Mission). Tranquebar was NOT ceded to France; it was sold by Denmark to Britain in 1845. Hence option 4 is incorrectly matched.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Tranquebar – Missionary and Cultural Significance]
options: Bartholomäus Ziegenbalg – First Protestant missionary at Tranquebar (1706)
Tranquebar – Site of the first Tamil printing press established by European missionaries
Heinrich Plütschau – Accompanied Ziegenbalg to Tranquebar as a co-missionary
Tranquebar Mission – Sponsored by the British East India Company
wrong_fact: The Tranquebar Mission (1706) was sponsored by the Danish King Frederick IV and supported by the Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge (SPCK) of England — NOT by the British East India Company. The British EIC was actually reluctant about missionary activities in its territories.
explanation: Ziegenbalg and Plütschau arrived at Tranquebar in 1706. Ziegenbalg established the first Tamil printing press and translated the New Testament into Tamil. The mission was sponsored by Danish King Frederick IV and the German Pietist Halle Mission, with support from SPCK (UK). The British East India Company did NOT sponsor the Tranquebar Mission; in fact, the Company often discouraged missionary work fearing it would disrupt trade relations. Hence option 4 is incorrectly matched.
